text:
deploy-bot: Preflight report for rollout v2.3.1 -> canary 5% eu-west. Checks: SLO smoke: PASS; Error budget check: OK; Autoscaler warmup: WARN (nodepool-canary-2 scaling lag); KV cache hit-rate: drop 28%. Release notes: https://redwood/release/v2.3.1; runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/deploy-preflight

sre-oncall: :eyes: seeing a small 429 spike on canary - 3m p95 1.2s, 429s ~0.6% but trending up over the last 5m

chris: logs show many gRPC stream resets from canary nodes, looks like disk pressure + slow pod startup on nodepool-canary-2. Scale-up latency is the suspect

maria: recommend PAUSE traffic shift and hold at 2.5% while we triage. Also propose pinning eu-west to v2.3.0 until we confirm the root cause

alex: +1 to pause. If autoscaler cannot keep up, fallback to smaller batch size or low-latency profile. Can ops flip runtime batching toggle?

priya: I can flip batching to the low-latency profile for canary, but I prefer pausing + pinning first to avoid user impact

deploy-bot: Actionable commands (copy-paste):
```
/deploy pause --rollout v2.3.1 --region eu-west
/rollout pin --region eu-west --version v2.3.0
/ops toggle batching --profile low-latency --region eu-west --target nodepool-canary-*
```

sre-oncall: Running the pause now

deploy-bot: Rollout paused by @sre-oncall at 1765554337. Canary traffic held at 2.5%. Pin command queued

chris: Starting nodepool diagnostics now, pulling dmesg and kube events from the affected nodes

maria: If we can't repro within 15m we can consider staged 1% increments. Hard stop: if 5xx/429 > 0.5% or p95 > 1s we rollback

priya: Quick test: flipping batching in canary test env gave ~50% drop in 429s. Encouraging but production still risky without pin

deploy-bot: Pin applied: eu-west -> v2.3.0 at 1765554440. Notifying #releases and creating incident if error budget dips

alex: TL;DR: pause + pin. I'll add an entry in the release notes about autoscaler warmup and an action item for infra to tune scale policies

maria: Created ticket INFRA-453: investigate nodepool warmup thresholds and reduce default initial batch size

chris: Quick diagnostic snippet from one canary node (OOM at 1765554385):
```
OOM killer: task gpt_worker invoked
Killed process 12345 (gpt_worker) total-vm: 1.2G
```

sre-oncall: keeping watch on dashboards and logs. Will re-open thread if we see regression. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Thread closed for active rollout; will reopen on new anomalies. Follow-up checklist: INFRA-453, release note update, rollback readiness doc update. :white_check_mark:
